messages:
Anika (PM): Quick sync — optimize toolkit roadmap planning. We need to slice Q3 work: batching/caching recommender, prompt-set regression detection, and a light eval harness for customers. Propose priority order and launch criteria.
Ravi (Staff SWE): +1. My gut: batching/caching recommender is highest impact for cost. Short win if we ship policy templates + telemetry.
Jenna (ML Eng): Agreed. Also need automated regression alerts tied to evals — we keep seeing prompt-set drift after model rollouts.
Marco (Product Ops): Customer asks: a few enterprise pilots want explicit action items (what to change in config) not just metrics. So recommender should output concrete config diffs.
Chris (Design): UX: show before/after token cost estimate and expected p95 latency change. Minimal UI mock: small card with "Apply recommendation" CTA + inline rationale.
Ravi (Staff SWE): Tech constraints: we need sample distribution of seq lengths + recent KV-cache hit-rate to surface good batching thresholds. Suggest phased approach:
```
Phase 0: offline suggestion engine (CSV input, CLI)
Phase 1: live recommender behind feature flag (read-only recommendations)
Phase 2: apply/recommend automation with rollback
```
Jenna (ML Eng): For regression detection: we should tie to prompt-set baselines. Minimal launch: weekly eval run, compare key metrics (ROUGE/EMB-sim/acceptance-rate), thresholded alerts.
Marco (Product Ops): Launch criteria for regressions: alerting must include example prompts where output changed, and an impact score (customer-visible traffic % affected).
Anika (PM): OK, let's draft OKRs:
- O1: Reduce served token cost by 12% for customers using recommender (Q3).
- O2: Detect >90% of prompt-set regressions before customer impact (Q3).
- O3: 3 pilot customers sign up for automated recommendations (end of quarter).
Ravi (Staff SWE): Q: how heavy is weekly eval? Can we run cheap proxy eval (embedding similarity + heuristics) to start vs full reference metrics?
Jenna (ML Eng): Yes — start with embedding-based similarity + simple heuristics for hallucination signals. Keep heavy evals for on-demand runs.
Chris (Design): For prompt-sets, UI needs to surface diff examples and a small histogram of metric drift. Keep it compact.
Marco (Product Ops): Risks: recommending overly aggressive batching that breaks latency SLOs. Mitigation: recommendations require simulated latency check against recent p95 trace and a safety cap.
Anika (PM): Scope negotiation: must-have for MVP: offline recommender + weekly regression alerts + small UI to inspect diffs. Nice-to-have: auto-apply recommendations, canaries, fine-grained cost forecasting.
Ravi (Staff SWE): Implementation note: store recommendation metadata as a small JSON blob with schema: model, route, suggested_batch_size, expected_token_savings, safety_margin_pct. Example: `{"model":"rwd-7b","route":"/generate","suggested_batch_size":8,"expected_token_savings":"14%","safety_margin_pct":20}`
ops-bot: deploy note: running weekly eval job scheduled Fri 03:00 UTC in staging -> job id 2024-07-05-eval-07
Jenna (ML Eng): Metrics to track post-launch: adoption rate (applied recommendations), realized token savings, false-positive rate for regression alerts, time-to-investigation.
Anika (PM): Action items:
- Ravi: prototype offline recommender by 1718870000 (2 weeks).
- Jenna: author regression detection spec + lightweight eval harness by 1718890000 (3 weeks).
- Marco: outreach to 5 pilot customers and pick 3 by next week.
- Chris: 1 small UI mock for review by end of week.
Ravi (Staff SWE): noted. I'll post PR with CLI tool and sample CSV format.
Marco (Product Ops): I'll run customer outreach today, drop list in #customer-success.
Chris (Design): I'll iterate on mock and attach to thread.
Anika (PM): Cool — we'll treat this as prioritized for Q3 backlog if prototypes look good. Revisit in next planning sync. :thumbsup:
